Terns spring mass-measurement timing check

Issue #7 - follow-up to issue #5 task 3, per Yosef

2026-09-20

1 Background

Yosef doesn’t always have time to weigh/measure every bird he catches - confirmed with Inbal that which birds get weighed when time is short is effectively random (whenever he has a free moment), not targeted at particular individuals, so that specific selection concern doesn’t need further checking here.

What this script checks instead: whether when within the spring season (Mar-May) the weighed birds were caught has drifted over the years, and if so, whether that drift could be inflating or masking the mass-decline trend already reported in issue #5 task 3 / issue #6.

Scope: spring-caught adults only (juveniles aren’t relevant here, since they’re caught in summer, not spring). Common Tern is split into breeder/non-breeder (same definitions as task 3), since #5 found a real mass difference between them. Little Tern is kept as a single “Adult” group, unsplit - #5 task 2 found no significant mass difference between Little Tern breeders and non-breeders under either definition (2b: p=0.32-0.62; 2c: p=0.61-0.77), so splitting it here would just be dividing an already small sample (n=184-224 per subgroup) for no analytical benefit.

2 Data loading

raw_dir <- "../data_raw"
if (!dir.exists(raw_dir)) raw_dir <- "data_raw"
stopifnot(dir.exists(raw_dir))

proc_dir <- "../data_processed"
if (!dir.exists(proc_dir)) proc_dir <- "data_processed"

out_dir <- "../output"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) out_dir <- "output"

ringing_path <- file.path(raw_dir, "ringing_data_raw.xlsx")
stopifnot(file.exists(ringing_path))

col_names_47 <- c(
  "CR1","RingReplace","Rec","RingPrefix","RingNum","Species","Sex","Age","Wing","Weight",
  "Date","Time","Place","Lat","Lon","Ringer","Country","Remarks","Net","CR2","Subsp","Tail","Head",
  "Breeding","CP1","CP2","CP3","CP4","Colour","D","M","OrigDate","OrigCountry","OrigLat","OrigLon","OrigAge",
  "OldCR1","OldCR2","OldCR3","OldMetal1","OldMetal2","OilHead","OilWings","OilUpperP","OilUnderP","OilLegs","OilSum"
)
raw <- read_excel(ringing_path, sheet = "Data", skip = 2, col_names = col_names_47)

terns <- raw %>%
  filter(Species %in% c("STEALB", "STEHIR")) %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(Date),
    month = month(Date),
    date = as.Date(Date),
    ring_id = paste0(trimws(RingPrefix), RingNum),
    is_new = is.na(Rec) | trimws(Rec) == "",
    species_label = ifelse(Species == "STEHIR", "Common Tern", "Little Tern")
  )

3 Building the spring-adult groups

Identical construction to issue #5 task 3 / 03_mass_trends.Rmd: confirmed breeder = any spring-caught adult (new ringing or recapture) also recorded in Jun/Jul of any year. day_of_season = days since March 1 of that year (spring window = Mar-May, so this runs roughly 0-91).

juvenile_ages <- c(1, 3)
summer_ring_ids_anyyear <- terns %>%
  filter(month %in% 6:7) %>%
  distinct(ring_id) %>%
  pull(ring_id)

spring_adults <- terns %>%
  filter(!(Age %in% juvenile_ages), !is.na(Weight), month %in% 3:5) %>%
  mutate(
    confirmed_breeder_anyyear = ring_id %in% summer_ring_ids_anyyear,
    group = case_when(
      species_label == "Little Tern" ~ "Adult",
      confirmed_breeder_anyyear ~ "Adult breeder",
      TRUE ~ "Adult non-breeder"
    ),
    group = factor(group, levels = c("Adult", "Adult non-breeder", "Adult breeder")),
    panel_label = factor(paste(species_label, group, sep = " - "),
                          levels = c("Common Tern - Adult non-breeder", "Common Tern - Adult breeder",
                                     "Little Tern - Adult")),
    day_of_season = as.numeric(date - as.Date(paste0(year, "-03-01")))
  )

kable(
  spring_adults %>% group_by(species_label, group) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), n_years = n_distinct(year), .groups = "drop"),
  caption = "Spring-adult weighed records by species and group"
)
Spring-adult weighed records by species and group
species_label group n n_years

Common Tern Adult breeder 490 16
Little Tern Adult 408 16

4 1. Does mass vary with day-of-season within spring?

Individual-level Weight ~ day_of_season regression, per species and group.

within_season_stats <- spring_adults %>%
  group_by(species_label, group, panel_label) %>%
  filter(n() >= 10) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    m <- lm(Weight ~ day_of_season, data = .x)
    s <- summary(m)
    tibble(
      n = nrow(.x),
      slope_g_per_day = round(coef(m)["day_of_season"], 4),
      se = round(s$coefficients["day_of_season", "Std. Error"], 4),
      p_value = signif(s$coefficients["day_of_season", "Pr(>|t|)"], 3),
      r_squared = round(s$r.squared, 4)
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

kable(within_season_stats, caption = "Weight ~ day_of_season, by species and group")
Weight ~ day_of_season, by species and group
species_label group panel_label n slope_g_per_day se p_value r_squared
Common Tern Adult non-breeder Common Tern - Adult non-breeder 1593 0.1310 0.0204 0.0000 0.0253
Common Tern Adult breeder Common Tern - Adult breeder 490 0.0847 0.0352 0.0166 0.0117
Little Tern Adult Little Tern - Adult 408 0.0192 0.0205 0.3490 0.0022 
sig_ws <- within_season_stats %>% filter(p_value < 0.05) %>% distinct(panel_label)
spring_adults_sig <- spring_adults %>% semi_join(sig_ws, by = "panel_label")

ggplot(spring_adults, aes(day_of_season, Weight, color = species_label)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(data = spring_adults_sig, method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~panel_label, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(title = "Mass vs. day-of-season within the spring window (Mar-May)",
       subtitle = "Trend line shown only where the day-of-season slope is significant (p<0.05)",
       x = "Day of season (days since Mar 1)", y = "Weight (g)") +
  theme_minimal()

5 2. Has the day-of-season of weighed birds shifted over the years?

Individual-level day_of_season ~ year regression, per species and group - tests whether recent years’ weighed birds are caught systematically earlier or later in the spring window than early years’.

date_shift_stats <- spring_adults %>%
  group_by(species_label, group, panel_label) %>%
  filter(n() >= 10, n_distinct(year) >= 3) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    m <- lm(day_of_season ~ year, data = .x)
    s <- summary(m)
    tibble(
      n = nrow(.x),
      n_years = n_distinct(.x$year),
      slope_days_per_year = round(coef(m)["year"], 3),
      se = round(s$coefficients["year", "Std. Error"], 3),
      p_value = signif(s$coefficients["year", "Pr(>|t|)"], 3)
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

kable(date_shift_stats, caption = "day_of_season ~ year, by species and group")
day_of_season ~ year, by species and group
species_label group panel_label n n_years slope_days_per_year se p_value
Common Tern Adult non-breeder Common Tern - Adult non-breeder 1593 16 -1.432 0.070 0.00000
Common Tern Adult breeder Common Tern - Adult breeder 490 16 -0.406 0.148 0.00635
Little Tern Adult Little Tern - Adult 408 16 -0.863 0.130 0.00000 
sig_ds <- date_shift_stats %>% filter(p_value < 0.05) %>% distinct(panel_label)
spring_adults_sig_ds <- spring_adults %>% semi_join(sig_ds, by = "panel_label")

ggplot(spring_adults, aes(year, day_of_season, color = species_label)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(data = spring_adults_sig_ds, method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~panel_label, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(title = "Day-of-season of weighed adults, by year",
       subtitle = "Trend line shown only where the year slope is significant (p<0.05)",
       x = "Year", y = "Day of season (days since Mar 1)") +
  theme_minimal()

6 3. Could the date shift explain (or mask) the mass-decline trend?

If mass changes by beta g per day-of-season (section 1), and the sampling date itself is shifting by delta days per year (section 2), the date shift alone would be expected to move the yearly mass average by beta * delta g/year - compare this implied contribution against the actual observed mass-decline slope from issue #5 task 3 (data_processed/mass_trends_stats.csv, raw mass) to see whether the date shift works with the decline (would partly explain it) or against it (the true decline may be understated). For Little Tern, the comparison uses task 3’s “All adults (unsplit)” slope, matching the unsplit Adult group used here.

observed_trend <- read.csv(file.path(proc_dir, "mass_trends_stats.csv")) %>%
  filter(group %in% c("Adult breeder", "Adult non-breeder", "All adults (unsplit)")) %>%
  select(species_label, group, observed_slope_g_per_year = slope_g_per_year, observed_p = p_value)

combined_check <- within_season_stats %>%
  select(species_label, group, panel_label, within_season_slope = slope_g_per_day, within_season_p = p_value) %>%
  inner_join(
    date_shift_stats %>% select(species_label, group, date_shift_slope = slope_days_per_year, date_shift_p = p_value),
    by = c("species_label", "group")
  ) %>%
  mutate(implied_contribution_g_per_year = round(within_season_slope * date_shift_slope, 4)) %>%
  mutate(observed_join_group = ifelse(species_label == "Little Tern", "All adults (unsplit)", as.character(group))) %>%
  inner_join(observed_trend, by = c("species_label" = "species_label", "observed_join_group" = "group")) %>%
  select(-observed_join_group) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_of_observed = round(100 * implied_contribution_g_per_year / observed_slope_g_per_year, 1),
    direction = ifelse(sign(implied_contribution_g_per_year) == sign(observed_slope_g_per_year),
                        "Same direction as decline (could partly explain it)",
                        "Opposite direction (works against the decline - true effect may be understated)")
  )

kable(combined_check, digits = 4,
      caption = "Implied contribution of the within-season date shift to the observed yearly mass trend")
Implied contribution of the within-season date shift to the observed yearly mass trend
species_label group panel_label within_season_slope within_season_p date_shift_slope date_shift_p implied_contribution_g_per_year observed_slope_g_per_year observed_p pct_of_observed direction
Common Tern Adult non-breeder Common Tern - Adult non-breeder 0.1310 0.0000 -1.432 0.0000 -0.1876 -0.173 0.0071 108.4 Same direction as decline (could partly explain it)
Common Tern Adult breeder Common Tern - Adult breeder 0.0847 0.0166 -0.406 0.0063 -0.0344 -0.554 0.0000 6.2 Same direction as decline (could partly explain it)
Little Tern Adult Little Tern - Adult 0.0192 0.3490 -0.863 0.0000 -0.0166 -0.164 0.0036 10.1 Same direction as decline (could partly explain it)

6.1 Interpretation

implied_contribution_g_per_year is what you’d expect the date shift alone to contribute to the yearly mass trend, given the within-season mass pattern. Compare its sign and magnitude (pct_of_observed) to the actual observed slope: if it points the same direction and is a meaningful share of the observed slope, part of the reported decline could be a timing artifact. If it points the opposite direction, or is a trivial share, the observed decline is not explained by within-season timing drift - if anything, a same-sign-opposing effect means the true condition decline could be slightly larger than what’s reported, since the timing shift is working against, not for, the observed pattern.

7 Save outputs

write.csv(within_season_stats, file.path(proc_dir, "spring_timing_within_season_stats.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(date_shift_stats, file.path(proc_dir, "spring_timing_date_shift_stats.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(combined_check, file.path(proc_dir, "spring_timing_combined_check.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("Wrote data_processed/spring_timing_within_season_stats.csv, spring_timing_date_shift_stats.csv, spring_timing_combined_check.csv\n")
